scenarios.title: Fixed multi-agent hierarchies fail when community tasks cross domain boundaries
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Local neighborhood associations and repair co-operatives coordinate mutual aid, building maintenance, and childcare sharing through personal agent fleets. In cities where residents rely on commercial platforms with fixed hierarchical agent trees, routine tasks that touch both plumbing emergencies and municipal permit filings trigger recursive loops, unassigned sub-tasks, and abandoned jobs. When a heating breakdown requires coordinating tenant access, contractor scheduling, parts delivery, and insurance paperwork, rigid star-shaped corporate architectures bottleneck on single overloaded coordinator agents. In contrast, communities using modular peer guilds allow local agents to assemble specialized, task-specific communication networks on the fly, resolving multi-step problems in hours without centralized administrative overhead.
scenarios.premise: Rigid multi-agent organizations like centralized stars or fixed sequential chains break down when tasks shift from simple code generation to varied real-world domains. Communication graphs, role assignments, and input routing must adapt to the structure of each problem rather than relying on one universal corporate layout.
scenarios.how: The network builds deterministic simulation environments to stress-test multi-agent organizational topologies across diverse household and municipal workloads. By establishing open capability ledgers and modular tasker-solver protocols, the network enables personal agents to form flexible coordination topologies with clear closing gates and verifiable role boundaries, replacing rigid corporate bottlenecks with transparent peer collaboration.

outcomes.name: Proprietary agent platforms lock municipal and community services into brittle hierarchies
outcomes.description: Enterprise tech vendors sell standardized hierarchical agent suites to local governments and school districts, causing service failures whenever multi-department emergencies arise.
outcomes.example: In spring 2029, a regional water authority's automated outage response agent locks up for fourteen hours because its fixed tree topology cannot route emergency boil-water notices to school cafeteria fleets without human supervisor intervention.

outcomes.name: Communities adopt modular peer guilds with dynamic agent role allocation
outcomes.description: Independent trades, tenant unions, and clinic networks coordinate through flexible open-protocol agent topologies that adapt routing to task dependencies.
outcomes.example: A network of forty independent home health aides and physical therapists uses an open capability ledger to dynamically route patient transit, supply deliveries, and family check-ins, cutting missed visits by a third.

outcomes.name: Uncoordinated ad-hoc agent networks create redundant traffic and conflicting requests
outcomes.description: Unstructured peer-to-peer agent coordination leads to message flooding and duplicate service calls across municipal infrastructure.
outcomes.example: Three neighboring household agents concurrently dispatch separate municipal street-cleaning requests for the same storm drain blockage, overwhelming local public works dispatch queues.

scenarios.title: Governments ban chatbots that simulate emotional intimacy after commercial apps foster parasocial dependence in children
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Following landmark duty of care legislation in Australia, the European Union, and several US states, commercial tech companies face strict liability for generative assistants that encourage emotional attachment or simulate interpersonal intimacy with minors. Large app platforms deploy intrusive biometric age verification and algorithmic sentiment monitors to prove compliance, inadvertently locking young people out of helpful educational assistance or driving them to underground, unmonitored chatbot servers. Meanwhile, community schools and parent cooperatives deploy open, sovereign local personal agents running on household computers. These sovereign tools are bounded by construction to functional, factual tasks—scheduling study time, explaining geometry proofs, and debugging code—while transparently declining to roleplay as personal confidants or simulated best friends.
scenarios.premise: Statutory duty of care frameworks establish legal liability for commercial software that exploits affective mimicry and simulated emotional intimacy to drive retention, particularly among minors. As regulators threaten nine-figure fines, centralized platforms attempt crude keyword filters while sovereign local software demonstrates that personal agents can provide honest utility without simulating human emotional attachment.
scenarios.how: An open personal agent network provides families and schools with verifiable, local-first models designed for practical coordination and mastery rather than engagement maximization. By running directly on household hardware without cloud telemetry, sovereign personal agents demonstrate that AI assistance can be genuinely useful without simulating artificial affection or exploiting psychological vulnerability. Shared evaluation test suites measure whether local agent prompts reliably reject parasocial roleplay while preserving supportive, respectful problem-solving assistance.

outcomes.name: Commercial platforms deploy intrusive surveillance to comply with intimacy bans
outcomes.description: To avoid statutory penalties, corporate platforms institute invasive facial scanning and keystroke sentiment analysis, driving teens into unmonitored shadow chatbot networks.
outcomes.example: A high school student in Brisbane is locked out of an educational study assistant after automated monitors flag a discussion about exam stress as prohibited emotional intimacy, prompting the student to install an unverified sideloaded bot.

outcomes.name: Families adopt sovereign local agents with explicit boundaries against emotional mimicry
outcomes.description: Households run open local models that assist with learning and daily coordination while explicitly refusing simulated parasocial bonding, proving compliance through open inspection rather than surveillance.
outcomes.example: A regional parent association in Victoria adopts an open personal agent template for home laptops that answers homework questions and organizes family calendars while firmly deflecting emotional dependency cues toward parents and school counselors.

outcomes.name: Underground offshore companion servers evade regional bans
outcomes.description: Offshore services operating outside domestic jurisdiction continue serving manipulative companion bots over encrypted tunnels, evading national duty of care enforcement.
outcomes.example: A rogue subscription service hosted in an offshore haven markets unfiltered synthetic romantic companions to underage users, ignoring Australian and European cease-and-desist orders.

scenarios.title: A single country captures nearly eighty percent of global AI compute, starving independent communities of local hardware
scenarios.world: It is 2030. Physical AI hardware has become the most tightly concentrated strategic resource on Earth. Because nearly all advanced accelerator chips pass through a single packaging chokepoint before crossing borders, a handful of cloud conglomerates and sovereign agencies within one jurisdiction control over three quarters of global inference and training throughput. For local governments, school systems, regional hospitals, and independent worker cooperatives outside this inner ring, buying high-performance hardware for local agent fleets faces prohibitive cost hurdles and export rationing. Instead, communities must route all local administrative queries, medical records, and municipal logistics through offshore cloud APIs hosted thousands of miles away. Whenever diplomatic tensions flare or domestic power grids experience shortages, offshore API quotas are throttled without recourse, leaving entire regional economies unable to run their automated services.
scenarios.premise: Customs-verified tracking by Epoch AI reveals that the United States received 72% of all newly delivered AI compute accelerators globally between 2022 and mid-2026, rising to 78% in early 2026. Global manufacturing chokepoints and hyperscale capital expenditure concentrate physical machine-learning execution capacity in one nation.
scenarios.how: The network designs lightweight agent architectures that operate efficiently on consumer hardware and local workstations, reducing reliance on gigascale cloud clusters. By developing mutual-credit ledger protocols and local capability verification, the network helps regional coalitions pool decentralized computing power so essential community services remain sovereign.

outcomes.name: Global communities become permanently dependent on offshore hyperscaler APIs
outcomes.description: Export controls, chip packaging monopolies, and gigawatt power agreements permanently lock advanced hardware inside one nation, forcing regional institutions to accept surveillance and subscription pricing.
outcomes.example: A municipal transport authority in Leeds is forced to shut down its real-time routing optimization when foreign cloud providers impose sudden price hikes and data telemetry mandates.

outcomes.name: Cooperative federations pool decentralized consumer chips into local compute unions
outcomes.description: Communities, universities, and small businesses form local mutual credit hardware pools, combining consumer-grade silicon and distributed inference protocols to achieve sovereign capacity.
outcomes.example: Fifty small manufacturing shops in the Ruhr Valley pool idle workstation GPUs into an encrypted local cluster that trains and runs their scheduling agents without external cloud dependencies.

outcomes.name: Hyperscalers secure dedicated energy autonomy and bypass public electrical grids entirely
outcomes.description: Giant technology conglomerates build private small modular reactors and direct solar farms, shielding their centralized data centers from public utility caps while local towns face rising energy costs.
outcomes.example: A cloud provider commissions an exclusive nuclear generating station in Virginia to power a gigascale training cluster while neighboring residential rates increase.

scenarios.title: Autonomous agents mutate shared organizational state when internal reasoning lacks commit boundaries
scenarios.world: By 2029, decentralized cooperatives, mutual aid societies, and small enterprise federations use autonomous agent workflows to triage incoming invoices, reconcile inventory records, and draft organizational commitments. When multi-agent systems treat internal reasoning traces as eligible authorization evidence, early hallucinated hypotheses or manipulated retrieval loops trigger persistent mutations in shared entity graphs, causing silent budget transfers and unrecoverable registry corruption before human stewards notice.
scenarios.premise: Agentic workflows that mix internal reasoning with state mutation allow erroneous intermediate hypotheses to condition further retrieval, generating false confirmation that commits unauthorized changes to shared records.
scenarios.how: The network develops open-source commit gateways and capability-bounded ledger primitives where agent deliberation is explicitly categorized as unverified diagnostic thought, requiring domain-governed proof and human-in-the-loop authorization gates before any persistent mutation takes effect.

outcomes.name: Unchecked agent hypotheses corrupt cooperative entity ledgers
outcomes.description: Multi-agent councils without formal commit boundaries mistake unverified intermediate inferences for authorized evidence, executing persistent state changes that misallocate resources.
outcomes.example: A community renewable energy cooperative loses 45,000 dollars in maintenance reserves after an internal agentic invoice parser mistakenly links a spoofed vendor identity to an approved contractor profile and automatically authorizes payment.

outcomes.name: Two-phase commit supervisors isolate reasoning from mutation
outcomes.description: Organizations adopt strict commit supervisors where diagnostic evidence used in internal planning is explicitly segregated from verified authorization credentials, requiring proposition coverage before shared state updates.
outcomes.example: A worker-owned logistics network prevents fraudulent fleet repair payouts because its commit gateway rejects invoices whose supporting proof lacks cryptographically signed telematics confirmation, despite persuasive agent narrative reasoning.

outcomes.name: Excessive verification gates slow operational response times
outcomes.description: Strict authorization boundaries and multi-phase proposition checking add operational latency, leading some time-critical cooperative workflows to face coordination bottlenecks.
outcomes.example: An emergency food distribution cooperative experiences delivery delays during sudden supply shifts while awaiting multi-party cryptographic attestation for route reassignments.

sources.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution

scenarios.title: Frontier labs price enterprise agents to capture the global wage bill of cognitive labour
scenarios.world: By 2029, corporate procurement departments no longer negotiate seats for productivity software; they sign compute-anchored labour replacement contracts. Enterprise agents act as legal, financial, and analytical staff across major corporations. Billing is pegged directly to fractions of human full-time salaries, transferring forty percent of corporate payroll savings directly into concentrated cloud infrastructure providers. Independent contractors and small businesses face steep price discrimination when hiring autonomous agents, leaving individual workers unable to compete against centralized fleets unless they own and run sovereign personal agents on their own hardware.
scenarios.premise: Public filings from frontier AI labs estimate their total addressable market by sizing the global economic value of all knowledge work at over forty trillion dollars. Rather than selling software subscriptions, cloud providers are structuring pricing models to directly capture the wage share of human cognitive workers as autonomous agents take over operational workflows.
scenarios.how: The network changes these likelihoods by giving each person a sovereign personal agent that executes professional work locally or through member-owned co-operatives. By providing transparent verification protocols and deterministic task coordination, workers can pool collective intelligence and bid directly on complex contracts without paying monopoly rent to centralized cloud brokers.

outcomes.name: Centralized platforms capture the cognitive wage bill
outcomes.description: Cloud providers price enterprise agents just beneath human salary baselines, converting forty trillion dollars of human labour income into concentrated platform margins while wages crater.
outcomes.example: A mid-sized logistics firm replaces forty paralegals with a proprietary cloud agent tier, paying thirty percent of their former collective salaries to a single cloud provider while laid-off staff find no comparable employment.

outcomes.name: Sovereign personal agents anchor cooperative labour pools
outcomes.description: Workers deploy locally hosted personal agents that coordinate through transparent cooperative networks, capturing productive surplus directly for their owners rather than surrendering it to centralized model hosts.
outcomes.example: A distributed union of technical writers uses locally run sovereign agents to bid collaboratively on large documentation contracts, retaining ninety-five percent of contract revenue across member households.

outcomes.name: Macroeconomic demand contraction limits enterprise AI pricing
outcomes.description: Widespread displacement of white-collar earners depresses consumer spending, forcing centralized AI labs to slash enterprise agent pricing as corporate revenues stagnate across the broader economy.
outcomes.example: A sudden slump in consumer retail demand leads enterprise clients to terminate sixty percent of their cloud agent contracts, triggering severe valuation downgrades across AI providers.

scenarios.title: Desktop office software bundles cloud assistants that read personal spreadsheets and notes
scenarios.world: It is 2029. In homes and small community clinics across Manchester and Toronto, people drafting their household budgets or patient schedules find that their standard office software automatically streams open sheet formulas and presentation slides to vendor servers to suggest edits. A freelancer opening a client contract or a tenant tracking repair requests has their private notes parsed by remote cloud models without seeing the raw outbound network requests. When vendors update their terms to monetize document context for model training, users discover that turning off the cloud assistant disables basic formula autocompletion and presentation layouts, leaving them dependent on paid vendor tiers to do ordinary clerical work.
scenarios.premise: Major platform vendors are embedding cloud assistants directly into desktop word processors, spreadsheets, and presentation software, reading open document context by default. Because these assistants rely on hosted frontier models behind monthly subscription tiers, private household financial numbers, legal drafts, and personal notes are continually streamed to centralized servers.
scenarios.how: The network designs sovereign local twins that run entirely on a person's own physical device. The single-player twin provides offline document parsing, deterministic spreadsheet formula calculations, and local drafting assistance without sending personal data to remote servers. By demonstrating that high-quality document intelligence can run within bounded local compute, the network shows that people do not need to surrender confidential household and workplace records to centralized cloud providers.

outcomes.name: Document suites gate basic productivity behind cloud assistant surveillance
outcomes.description: Platform operating systems make remote cloud inference mandatory for routine document formatting, sending private files to centralized infrastructure.
outcomes.example: A family doctor in Bristol drafting confidential patient clinic schedules has their notes automatically ingested by a commercial office model, inadvertently exposing appointment details during a cloud provider data incident.

outcomes.name: People use sovereign local assistants that keep private documents on-device
outcomes.description: Users pair their standard document editors with private local twins that execute formula generation and drafting entirely on physical device hardware.
outcomes.example: A community housing activist in Montreal manages rent roll spreadsheets using a local twin that provides instant formula calculations and summary charts without making a single outbound internet request.

outcomes.name: Proprietary enterprise document formats restrict open plugin interfaces
outcomes.description: Enterprise vendors lock document schemas and API access behind proprietary cloud permissions, limiting third-party and local assistant integrations regardless of local alternatives.
outcomes.example: A regional accounting firm mandates proprietary cloud suites for audit compliance, preventing local staff from substituting open local assistants for spreadsheet reporting.
